review_notes: I read the whole target file and the downstream uses of unitTarget, targetStep and datumTarget in HardSphere, mainly PhysicalVertex, PhysicalRouteGeometry and PhysicalCollision. The file has no @[simp] declarations. Both findings are missing-simp-lemma issues: the definitions are unfolded ad hoc downstream because no characterizing lemmas exist. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether the suggested lemmas would be closed by simp unaided. Orientation and cycle concerns don't arise, because there are no competing or looping rules. I found nothing else in the rubric's scope.

findings.excerpt: Set.pi Set.univ (fun j ↦ Set.Ico (c j-1/2) (c j+1/2))
findings.problem: unitTarget is a bare def with no membership characterization. Every proof that needs the coordinatewise description unfolds it and rebuilds its own simp set: `simp [unitTarget]` at line 91 here, and `simp only [unitTarget,mem_pi,mem_univ,forall_const,mem_Ico,Pi.sub_apply,Pi.add_apply]` in unitTarget_sub in PhysicalVertex. The canonical form `u ∈ unitTarget c ↔ ∀ j, c j - 1/2 ≤ u j ∧ u j < c j + 1/2` is not available as a simp lemma. Callers have to unfold the definition, which exposes Set.pi/Ico internals. In datumTarget_measurable the `he` rewrite exists only to push this characterization through.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma mem_unitTarget {c u : Point} : u ∈ unitTarget c ↔ ∀ j, c j - 1/2 ≤ u j ∧ u j < c j + 1/2` (proved by `simp [unitTarget]`). Use it in the `he` step of datumTarget_measurable and in unitTarget_sub, and make unitTarget_radius a consequence of it. Keep `unitTarget` itself non-simp so it is not unfolded.
findings.benefit: Membership goals simplify to one stable coordinatewise normal form. The ad hoc simp sets in this file and in unitTarget_sub collapse to `simp`, and later proofs no longer depend on how unitTarget is defined.

findings.excerpt: if j.val=0 then 0 else fun k ↦
findings.problem: targetStep has no simp lemmas for its special values. The callers' proofs unfold the whole if-then-else just to evaluate `targetStep 0`, and the positive/negative cases are separate non-simp lemmas elsewhere. Examples: `simpa [hv,targetStep,B] using h` in vertexTarget_volume, and `simp only [routeCellPeriod,targetStep,Fin.val_zero,↓reduceIte,add_zero,sub_self]` in PhysicalRouteGeometry. Both only need `targetStep 0 = 0`. Passing the definition to simp exposes the nested ifs and `%`/`/` arithmetic, so the unfolding is brittle and noisy.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma targetStep_zero : targetStep 0 = 0 := by simp [targetStep]` next to the definition. Optionally also move targetStep_positive and targetStep_negative here with `Fin`-literal statements. Then the callers can use `simp [hv, B]` and `simp [routeCellPeriod]` without unfolding targetStep.
findings.benefit: Terms like `anchorPoint v + targetStep 0` normalize to `anchorPoint v`, as in datumTarget and the PhysicalCollision subset claim. Downstream simp calls stop depending on the internal if-then-else encoding of targetStep.
